# VextJS Complete English Documentation Index

> Generated from every public English documentation source. Each canonical URL appears exactly once with its source-derived summary.

## English documentation

- [VextJS](https://vextjs.github.io/): AI-first full-stack Node.js framework for APIs and server-rendered React pages, with typed contracts, OpenAPI, and machine-readable docs.
- [Access Log middleware](https://vextjs.github.io/api/access-log): Access Log uses app.logger to record the method, path, status, downstream processing time, and client IP for requests that reach the middleware. This page covers the seven config.accessLog fields and their boundaries. For business logs, see the Logger Guide.
- [Application Instance](https://vextjs.github.io/api/app): This page details the complete API of the VextJS application instance VextApp, including built-in modules, extension methods, life cycle hooks and startup functions.

- [Scheduled Jobs API](https://vextjs.github.io/api/jobs): This page is the reference for public signatures, validation and errors. The Jobs guide covers configuration, development, deployment and troubleshooting; the contract defines execution guarantees.
- [Plugin API](https://vextjs.github.io/api/plugin-api): This page details the plug-in system API of VextJS, including plug-in definitions, middleware definition helper functions and related types.
- [Route definition](https://vextjs.github.io/api/route-definition): This page details the route definition API of VextJS, including defineRoutes, routing options, parameter validation, middleware references and document configuration.
- [Test tools](https://vextjs.github.io/api/testing-api): This page documents createTestApp, TestApp, TestRequest, TestRequestBuilder, TestResponse, and createTestJobScheduler. See the Testing guide for a complete business fixture and execution steps; use this page for signatures, defaults, and execution boundaries.

- [SSR](https://vextjs.github.io/frontend/ssr): Server-side rendering is the default Vext page path. The route handler owns the URL and prepares the data; the frontend page owns the React view.

- [Cluster multi-process](https://vextjs.github.io/guide/cluster): VextJS uses one Master to manage multiple HTTP Workers. Each Worker has its own application instance and listens on the same service port. The Master starts and replaces Workers, checks heartbeats, and coordinates rolling reloads.

- [Rate Limiting](https://vextjs.github.io/guide/rate-limit): VextJS global rate limiting is disabled by default.
